sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: A person can be identified with a short noun phrase after the appropriate form of lenni.

Look closely: there’s no word for ‘is’ anywhere in Ő egy ember, even though egy ember is doing exactly that job. Present-tense Hungarian drops the copula when a noun phrase identifies who or what someone is — the noun does all the work van would do elsewhere. Try reading it aloud as ‘He a person’ in your head; that’s literally the skeleton you’re building on.
